Series::ceil¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::ceil() const -> Series
Series& Series::ceil_()

What It Does¶

ceil() rounds each element upward to the least integer value that is greater than or equal to that element.

This is an elementwise transform:

  • shape is preserved

  • dtype stays numeric

  • each lane is processed independently

For negative numbers, “upward” still means toward positive infinity. That is why -1.2 becomes -1 rather than -2.

Returns¶

Series A new Series whose elements have been rounded upward.

Gradient¶

Away from integer jump points, ceil(x) is locally constant, so its derivative is 0.

That is the right mental model for reverse-mode too: once a scalar objective passes through ceil(), small perturbations to the input do not change the rounded value until an integer boundary is crossed.

In-Place Form¶

ceil_() is the in-place sibling of ceil(): it computes the same result and writes it back into self directly — mutating it (and any other handle sharing the same storage) instead of allocating a new Series — then returns a reference to self.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.2, -1.2, 2.0});

auto& ref = x.ceil_();
std::cout << "x=" << x << "\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "same object: " << (&ref == &x);

Output¶

x=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[2, -1, 2]
same object: true

Examples¶

Example 1. Negative and positive values both round toward positive infinity.

std::cout << pluss::make_series({-1.2, -0.1, 0.0, 1.2, 2.1}).ceil();

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[-1, -0, 0, 2, 3]

The -0 display is still zero numerically. It is just the signed floating representation surfacing in the printout.

Example 2. Reverse-mode sensitivity is zero through the rounded lanes in this ordinary case.

auto x = pluss::make_series({-1.2, 0.0, 3.8});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

auto y = x.ceil();
y.sum().reverse();

std::cout << "out=" << y << "\n";
std::cout << "dL_dx=" << x.sensitivity();

Output¶

out=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-1, 0, 4]
dL_dx=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 0, 0]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • ceil() is not rounding-to-nearest; it always moves upward.

  • Negative values can move toward zero rather than away from it.

  • The transform is discontinuous at integers.

Summary¶

Use ceil() when every value should be promoted to the next admissible integer ceiling, with exact integers left unchanged.

See Also¶

  • Series::floor: rounds downward instead.

  • Series::round: rounds to the nearest integer instead of always upward.

  • Series::trunc: discards the fractional part toward zero.
